scenario: Discussing weekend plans with a friend
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Often used with 'en' or infinitive to express intention.

vocabulary.translation: to meet / to arrange to meet
vocabulary.note: Refers to making plans with someone.
Common for sequencing events.
Here means 'time'.
Feminine noun.
Also used as a filler (well...).
Introduces a reason.
Contrast conjunction.
Also used in 'hasta luego' (see you later).
Agrees with noun: mismo/misma.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Qué piensas hacer este fin de semana?
dialogue.translation: What are you planning to do this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No tengo mucho tiempo, pero quiero quedar contigo el sábado.
dialogue.translation: I don't have much time, but I want to meet up with you on Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¡Bueno! Podemos ir al cine y luego tomar algo.
dialogue.translation: Great! We can go to the movies and then grab a drink.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Mejor el domingo, porque el sábado trabajo toda la semana, ya sabes.
dialogue.translation: Better on Sunday, because on Saturday I work all week, you know.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Vale, el domingo a la misma hora que siempre.
dialogue.translation: Okay, Sunday at the same time as always.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Perfecto, hasta luego.
dialogue.translation: Perfect, see you later.

key_phrases.translation: What are you planning to do?

scenario: Returning a faulty item at a shop
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Use 'devolver' for returning goods to a shop.
Male noun: 'el problema'.
Often used in past tense 'compré' (I bought).
Male noun: 'el dinero'.
Irregular; used in 'tener que' (to have to).
Agrees in gender: 'otro' / 'otra'.
Indefinite pronoun.
Used in 'me parece' (it seems to me).
Connector to add information.
Invariable in gender.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hola, quiero devolver esta lámpara que compré ayer. Tiene un problema.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I want to return this lamp that I bought yesterday. It has a problem.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro, ¿me puede decir qué le pasa? ¿Tiene el recibo?
dialogue.translation: Of course, can you tell me what's wrong with it? Do you have the receipt?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, aquí tiene el recibo. No funciona bien y además no trae el cable.
dialogue.translation: Yes, here is the receipt. It doesn't work well and also it doesn't come with the cable.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Lo siento, pero necesito ver el cable para cambiarla. ¿Le parece bien si le devolvemos el dinero?
dialogue.translation: I'm sorry, but I need to see the cable to exchange it. Would it be okay if we refund your money?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Prefiero llevar otro modelo. ¿Tienen algo más moderno?
dialogue.translation: I prefer to take another model. Do you have something more modern?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, tenemos varias opciones. Es importante que usted quede contento, y además le haremos un descuento.
dialogue.translation: Yes, we have several options. It's important that you are satisfied, and also we'll give you a discount.

scenario: Booking a table at a restaurant by phone

vocabulary.note: Common for booking tables, rooms, etc.
In restaurant context, 'una mesa para dos' = a table for two.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buenas tardes, Restaurante El Sol. ¿En qué puedo ayudarle?
dialogue.translation: Good afternoon, El Sol Restaurant. How can I help you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hola, quiero reservar una mesa para esta noche, solo dos personas.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I want to reserve a table for tonight, just two people.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perfecto. ¿A qué hora le gustaría la mesa? ¿Y cuando llegue, me puede confirmar su nombre?
dialogue.translation: Perfect. What time would you like the table? And when you arrive, can you confirm your name?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: A las ocho, por favor. Mi nombre es Laura Gómez.
dialogue.translation: At eight, please. My name is Laura Gómez.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Muy bien, Laura. Una mesa para dos a las ocho. ¿Quiere algo más?
dialogue.translation: Very well, Laura. A table for two at eight. Would you like anything more?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, gracias, eso es todo. Hasta luego.
dialogue.translation: No, thank you, that's all. See you later.

scenario: Describing symptoms at a pharmacy
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Used here as 'me siento' (I feel).
Often used with 'tener' (to have pain).
In 'hace dos días' means 'two days ago'.
Note: 'porque' is not in the avoid list, but it's common.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Me siento muy mal desde ayer, tengo dolor de cabeza y un poco de fiebre.
dialogue.translation: I feel very bad since yesterday, I have a headache and a little fever.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Cuánto tiempo hace que tienes fiebre? ¿Ha empezado hoy?
dialogue.translation: How long have you had a fever? Did it start today?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Empezó hace dos días, y no puedo dormir bien porque me duele mucho la cabeza.
dialogue.translation: It started two days ago, and I can't sleep well because my head hurts a lot.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entiendo. ¿Toma algo para el dolor?
dialogue.translation: I understand. Are you taking anything for the pain?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No, nada. ¿Qué me recomienda para dormir mejor y bajar la fiebre?
dialogue.translation: No, nothing. What do you recommend for me to sleep better and lower the fever?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Le doy un medicamento para la fiebre y el dolor. Tómelo cada ocho horas, y si no se siente bien en dos días, vaya al médico.
dialogue.translation: I'll give you a medicine for the fever and pain. Take it every eight hours, and if you don't feel well in two days, go to the doctor.

scenario: Talking about your hometown to a visitor

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hola, bienvenido a mi ciudad. Yo vivo aquí desde niño.
dialogue.translation: Hello, welcome to my city. I have lived here since I was a child.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Gracias. ¿Es un lugar grande o pequeño?
dialogue.translation: Thank you. Is it a big or small place?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No es muy grande, pero me gusta porque todo está cerca.
dialogue.translation: It is not very big, but I like it because everything is close.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Y el centro? ¿Está lejos de aquí?
dialogue.translation: And the center? Is it far from here?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No, está a cinco minutos. La calle principal es muy bonita.
dialogue.translation: No, it's five minutes away. The main street is very pretty.

scenario: Changing a reservation at a hotel

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Buenos días, necesito cambiar mi reserva para otra fecha.
dialogue.translation: Good morning, I need to change my reservation for another date.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro, señor. ¿Qué fecha nueva le gustaría?
dialogue.translation: Of course, sir. What new date would you like?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Puedo cambiar mi habitación para mañana por la noche?
dialogue.translation: Can I change my room for tomorrow night?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Déjame ver... Sí, tenemos una habitación disponible para mañana.
dialogue.translation: Let me see... Yes, we have a room available for tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perfecto. ¿Puedo confirmar el cambio ahora?
dialogue.translation: Perfect. Can I confirm the change now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, cliente. Su reserva está actualizada. Gracias por esperar.
dialogue.translation: Yes, guest. Your reservation is updated. Thank you for waiting.

scenario: Asking for advice on what to buy
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Irregular comparative of 'bueno'.
Common in advice phrases like 'buena idea'.
Used with direct object: 'regalar algo a alguien'.
Also 'quizás'. Often followed by subjunctive.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quiero regalar algo a mi hermana, pero no sé qué comprar. ¿Tienes alguna idea?
dialogue.translation: I want to give something to my sister, but I don't know what to buy. Do you have any idea?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quizá un libro sea fácil y seguro, a ella le gusta leer.
dialogue.translation: Perhaps a book is easy and safe, she likes to read.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, pero quiero algo más especial, no un libro cada año.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but I want something more special, not a book every year.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Tal vez una bufanda hecha a mano, aunque requiere un poco de tiempo.
dialogue.translation: Maybe a handmade scarf, although it requires a bit of time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No tengo mucho tiempo, quizás mejor algo de tecnología.
dialogue.translation: I don't have much time, maybe better something tech.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entonces unos auriculares inalámbricos serían una buena opción, estoy seguro.
dialogue.translation: Then wireless headphones would be a good option, I'm sure.

scenario: Talking about past holidays
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Use 'pasar' + time expression to say how you spent a period.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Cómo pasaste las vacaciones?
dialogue.translation: How did you spend the holidays?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Viajé a la playa con mi familia. El primer día hizo mucho sol.
dialogue.translation: I traveled to the beach with my family. The first day was very sunny.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y qué hiciste en el mar?
dialogue.translation: And what did you do in the sea?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Nadamos y descansamos. Todo fue bueno, pero después llovió un poco.
dialogue.translation: We swam and rested. Everything was good, but afterwards it rained a bit.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿También visitaste algún pueblo cerca?
dialogue.translation: Did you also visit any town nearby?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, fuimos a un pueblo y comimos muy bien. También compramos recuerdos.
dialogue.translation: Yes, we went to a town and ate very well. We also bought souvenirs.

scenario: Discussing what you did last weekend
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Used for spending time: 'pasar el fin de semana'
Common for going out socially

vocabulary.translation: to meet up, to arrange to meet
vocabulary.note: In Spain, 'quedar con amigos' = meet up with friends
Masculine; feminine 'amiga'
Often used with 'ir al cine'
Compound noun, masculine
Context: 'estar aburrido' = to be bored; 'ser aburrido' = to be boring
Used for enjoyable activities

Note: 'porque' (one word) = because; 'por qué' = why

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Qué hiciste el fin de semana? ¿Saliste con amigos?
dialogue.translation: What did you do the weekend? Did you go out with friends?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, el sábado quedé con unos amigos y fuimos al cine a ver una película de acción.
dialogue.translation: Yes, on Saturday I met up with some friends and we went to the cinema to see an action movie.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Y qué tal la película? ¿Fue divertida o un poco aburrida?
dialogue.translation: And how was the movie? Was it fun or a bit boring?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Fue muy divertida, pero luego el domingo pasé el día en casa, porque estaba cansado.
dialogue.translation: It was very fun, but then on Sunday I spent the day at home, because I was tired.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¡Qué bien! Yo también salí, pero fui a un parque, y luego comí con mi familia.
dialogue.translation: How nice! I also went out, but I went to a park, and then I ate with my family.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Suena divertido. El próximo fin de semana podemos quedar para hacer algo juntos.
dialogue.translation: Sounds fun. Next weekend we can meet up to do something together.

key_phrases.translation: to spend the day at home
How was it? / How's it going?

scenario: Planning a birthday party

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.translation: Yes, we can celebrate on Saturday. Who do you want to invite?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Voy a invitar a mis amigos del trabajo, y también a sus primos.
dialogue.translation: I'm going to invite my friends from work, and also her cousins.

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.translation: Perfect. I can buy the cake and the drinks.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Genial. ¿Y quién va a traer el regalo para Ana?
dialogue.translation: Great. And who is going to bring the gift for Ana?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Podemos comprarlo juntos para que la fiesta sea muy alegre.

scenario: Asking about public transport routes

vocabulary.note: Used with 'a' to indicate destination.

vocabulary.translation: to get off, to go down

Feminine noun.
Also 'bus' in informal Spanish.
Indicates direction.
Demonstrative adverb of place.
Often used in questions about quantity or duration.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perdón, ¿sabe usted qué autobús debo tomar para llegar al centro?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, do you know which bus I should take to get to the center?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, tome el autobús número 7 que va hacia el centro. Debe bajarse en la parada de la plaza.
dialogue.translation: Yes, take bus number 7 that goes towards the center. You should get off at the square stop.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Cuánto tiempo tarda en llegar desde aquí?
dialogue.translation: How long does it take to get here from here?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Unos veinte minutos, pero depende del tráfico. También puede tomar el metro si tiene prisa.
dialogue.translation: About twenty minutes, but it depends on traffic. You can also take the metro if you're in a hurry.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Vale, entonces bajo en la siguiente parada, ¿verdad?
dialogue.translation: Okay, so I get off at the next stop, right?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, pero no olvide que debe pulsar el botón antes de bajar, o el autobús no se detiene.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but don't forget that you must press the button before getting off, or the bus won't stop.

key_phrases.translation: to get off at the stop

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.translation: Good morning, can you tell me how many years of work experience you have?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, tengo cinco años de experiencia, y durante ese tiempo trabajé en dos empresas diferentes.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I have five years of experience, and during that time I worked in two different companies.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Muy bien. ¿Qué sabe hacer usted solo en su trabajo, sin ayuda?
dialogue.translation: Very well. What can you do alone in your job, without help?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Puedo hacer todo lo necesario, porque aprendí rápido en mi último empleo.
dialogue.translation: I can do everything necessary, because I learned quickly in my last job.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perfecto. Después de esta entrevista, ¿tiene alguna pregunta para nosotros?
dialogue.translation: Perfect. After this interview, do you have any question for us?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, ¿podría decirme si el equipo también trabaja los sábados?
dialogue.translation: Yes, could you tell me if the team also works on Saturdays?

scenario: Discussing food preferences at dinner
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Used with indirect object pronouns (me, te, le); literally 'to be pleasing to'.
Regular -er verb; also used as a noun 'el comer' (food/eating).
Stem-changing (e>ie); very common for expressing desires.
Feminine noun; often used in general statements like 'otra cosa' (something else).
As an adverb means 'little/not much'; as an adjective agrees in gender/number.
Often used with 'no' in double negatives: 'no... nunca'.
Opposite of 'nunca'; frequently used with present tense for habits.
Used to agree with a negative statement; often paired with 'no'.
Indefinite pronoun; in questions it often means 'anything'.
As a pronoun: 'todo' = everything; as a determiner: 'todo el...' = all the...

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Qué quieres comer esta noche? ¿Te gusta algo en especial?
dialogue.translation: What do you want to eat tonight? Do you like anything in particular?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No tengo mucha hambre, pero nunca digo que no a una buena pasta. ¿Y tú?
dialogue.translation: I'm not very hungry, but I never say no to good pasta. And you?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: A mí me encanta la pasta, pero siempre pido algo con verduras porque me gusta comer sano.
dialogue.translation: I love pasta, but I always order something with vegetables because I like to eat healthy.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¡Ah! Pues yo prefiero la carne. No me gusta mucho el pescado, y tampoco las verduras solas.
dialogue.translation: Ah! Well, I prefer meat. I don't like fish much, and I don't like vegetables alone either.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entonces pedimos una pizza con jamón y champiñones. Así comemos algo los dos, ¿no?
dialogue.translation: Then let's order a pizza with ham and mushrooms. That way we both eat something, right?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¡Perfecto! Pero solo quiero un poco, porque luego quiero probar el postre. Todo se ve muy rico aquí.
dialogue.translation: Perfect! But I only want a little, because later I want to try dessert. Everything looks very tasty here.

scenario: Asking for help with a computer issue
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Common for starting a device
Used for machines, plans, etc.
Also means 'mouse' (animal).
Can be a physical button or on-screen.

vocabulary.translation: to turn off, to shut down

vocabulary.note: As adverb: 'rápidamente' (but 'rápido' is common informally).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mi computadora está muy lenta y a veces no funciona. ¿Puedes ayudarme?
dialogue.translation: My computer is very slow and sometimes it doesn't work. Can you help me?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro. Primero, intenta apagar el equipo y encenderlo de nuevo.
dialogue.translation: Sure. First, try to turn off the computer and turn it on again.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ya lo hice, pero el problema sigue. Ahora la pantalla está en negro.
dialogue.translation: I already did that, but the problem continues. Now the screen is black.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: ¿Revisaste el ratón y el teclado? A veces el botón de encendido no responde.
dialogue.translation: Did you check the mouse and the keyboard? Sometimes the power button doesn't respond.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sí, pero el teclado no responde rápido. ¿Qué hago?
dialogue.translation: Yes, but the keyboard doesn't respond quickly. What do I do?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Entonces, intenta apagar todo otra vez y espera un minuto antes de encender.
dialogue.translation: Then, try to turn everything off again and wait a minute before turning on.

scenario: Renting an apartment (first inquiry)
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Spanish

vocabulary.note: Common in Spain for 'apartment'; in Latin America often 'departamento'.
Refers to the price or the act of renting.
Used with 'de' to mean 'near to'.
Usually a bedroom or any room in a house.
Common for time periods in rentals.
Refers to the surface of the floor, not a story (which is 'planta').
Can mean natural light or electricity.
Regular -ar verb.
Used before a singular noun.
Irregular conjugation; essential verb.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hola, llamo por el piso que anunciaron. ¿Está todavía libre?
dialogue.translation: Hello, I'm calling about the apartment you advertised. Is it still available?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, está libre. ¿Necesita más información?
dialogue.translation: Yes, it's available. Do you need more information?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Cuál es el alquiler por mes?
dialogue.translation: What is the rent per month?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: El alquiler es de 600 euros cada mes. Tiene dos habitaciones y mucha luz.
dialogue.translation: The rent is 600 euros each month. It has two rooms and lots of light.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Está cerca del metro?
dialogue.translation: Is it near the metro?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, está muy cerca, y el suelo es de madera. ¿Quiere verlo?
dialogue.translation: Yes, it's very close, and the floor is wooden. Would you like to see it?
